# =============================================================================
# tessera-term: terminal modes (DECSET/DECRST, SM/RM, DECKPAM, kitty keyboard)  (issue #8, wave 6)
# crates/tessera-term/tests/fixtures/modes_spec.txt   (spec-researcher output; rows corrected by the implementer are marked
# `IMPLEMENTER CORRECTION (#8)` in a note)
#
# Same machine-readable layout as decstr_spec.txt / csi_spec.txt (### ID / size / step / cite / note /
# screen / cursor / pending_wrap / requests / scrollback), parsed by tests/spec/mod.rs. Extra keys the shared
# parser ignores and tests/modes.rs must assert by hand because render_screen cannot show them:
#     modes:     expected `Terminal::modes()` fields that DIFFER from Modes::default() after the whole
#                script ("default" = all defaults: auto_wrap, cursor_visible true, rest off/None/Default)
#     kbd:       expected `Terminal::keyboard_modes()` fields that differ from default
#     region:    expected grid.scroll_region(): "full" or "top..=bottom" 0-based
#     saved:     expected saved cursor of the ACTIVE screen "(row,col) wrap=<bool> origin=<bool>"  (hand-asserted)
#     screen_is: "main" | "alt" -- which screen is active at the end (Modes::alt_screen)
#     main:      expected rendered rows of the main screen when the active screen is the alternate one
#     flags:     xterm-quirk | decision | control | negative | unverified
# `control` cases run the setup WITHOUT the mode sequence and prove the later assertion is not vacuous.
# Cursor is 0-based (row,col). render_screen puts `|` AFTER the cursor's cell; a row ending in `\` is soft-wrapped.
# `set auto_wrap|insert_mode true|false` is the Terminal seam kept by the brief.
#
# PRIMARY SOURCES (read from source in this run; line numbers refer to the files as fetched 2026-10-28)
#   [CTL]  xterm ctlseqs  https://invisible-island.net/xterm/ctlseqs/ctlseqs.html   (XTerm Patch #411, 2026/08/23)
#   [XT]   xterm source, https://github.com/ThomasDickey/xterm-snapshots (master, charproc.c $XTermId 1.2134 2026/10/11)
#            charproc.c  dpmodes()  L7494..L8010   (DECSET/DECRST dispatcher; CASE_DECSET = dpmodes(bitset),
#                                                   CASE_DECRST = dpmodes(bitclr))
#            charproc.c  set_column_mode L7463, really_set_mousemode L7432, ToAlternate/FromAlternate/SwitchBufs
#                        L9529..L9590, ReallyReset L14355..L14560, resetMargins L1372, CASE_CUP/VPA/HPA/VPR/HPR L3943..L3980
#            cursor.c    CursorSet L68, CursorUp/Down, CursorSave2 L398, CursorRestoreFlags L467, DECSC_FLAGS L461
#            util.c      ClearScreen L2356
#   [ET]   esctest2 https://github.com/ThomasDickey/esctest2/tree/master/esctest/tests/  (decset.py, save_restore_cursor.py, vpa.py ...)
#   [DEC]  VT510 RM https://vt100.net/docs/vt510-rm/   (DECOM.html, DECAWM.html, DECTCEM.html, DECCOLM.html, LNM.html, IRM.html, DECSTR.html)
#   [KT]   kitty keyboard protocol https://sw.kovidgoyal.net/kitty/keyboard-protocol/ ; kitty/screen.c
#   [CNT]  Contour synchronized output https://github.com/contour-terminal/vt-extensions/blob/master/synchronized-output.md
#
# THE CENTRAL FACT FOR DECOM (verified in [XT] cursor.c CursorSet L68..L100 and charproc.c L3943..L3980)
#   Every absolute positioning sequence (CUP, HVP, VPA, HPA, VPR, HPR) ends in CursorSet(screen,row,col,xw->flags).
#   When flags&ORIGIN: row += top_marg and is clamped to bot_marg; col += lft_marg, clamped to rgt_marg.
#   CursorSet ALWAYS calls ResetWrap(screen) (pending wrap cleared) -- also for DECOM set/reset itself.
#   => VPA is origin-relative in xterm (esctest vpa.py "IgnoresOriginMode" asserts on the DSR CPR answer, which xterm
#      reports origin-relative, so the test name is misleading; see decision D-VPA).
#   CUU/CUD (cursor.c CursorUp/CursorDown) are NOT origin-dependent: they clamp to the margin only when the cursor starts
#      inside/below it, with or without DECOM.
# =============================================================================

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- DECOM (?6)

### DECOM01_set_homes_to_region_top
size: 6x10
step: feed \x1b[3;5r\x1b[6;6H\x1b[?6hX
cite: [XT] charproc.c L7598 `case srm_DECOM: (*func)(&xw->flags, ORIGIN); CursorSet(screen,0,0,xw->flags);` -> row = 0 + top_marg; [CTL] "CSI ? 6 h  Origin Mode (DECOM)"; [DEC] DECOM.html ("cursor moves to the home position ... within the margins")
note: DECSTBM 3;5 (rows 2..4 0-based) then DECSET 6 homes to the region's top-left, not the screen's. X lands at (2,0).

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- Alternate screen (47 / 1047 / 1048 / 1049)
# xterm facts (charproc.c dpmodes L7732..L7771; ToAlternate/FromAlternate L9529..L9560; SwitchBufs L9562):
#   47   set: ToAlternate(clearFirst=False)      reset: FromAlternate(False)                    -- no clear either way
#   1047 set: ToAlternate(False)                 reset: `if (whichBuf) ClearScreen; FromAlternate`  -- clears alt on the way OUT
#   1048 set: CursorSave (DECSC)                 reset: CursorRestore (DECRC)         (only when titeInhibit is off)
#   1049 set: CursorSave; ToAlternate; ClearScreen   reset: FromAlternate; CursorRestore
#   ToAlternate/FromAlternate are no-ops when already on / already off the alternate screen, but the OTHER calls in the arm still run:
#   1049 set on the alt screen still does CursorSave (into the ALT slot, sc[whichBuf]) and ClearScreen; 1049 reset on the main screen
#   still does CursorRestore (main slot). None of them touches the margins, the cursor position (except 1049-reset's restore),
#   the pen, or do_wrap (except ClearScreen's ResetWrap). Alt-screen lines are NOT preserved by Tessera's Grid (fresh blank each entry).
#   kitty (screen.c set_mode_from_const L2056): `if (val && on main) toggle ... else if (!val && on alt) toggle`: strict no-ops when already there; no clear.
#   Alacritty (term/mod.rs L1946, L2009): same guard; swap_alt() copies the primary cursor to the alt grid and RESETS alt contents on entry,
#   swaps the kitty keyboard stacks, does not touch the scroll region.

### ALT01_1049_set_enters_alt_blank_cursor_kept

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- DECCOLM (?3) and DECSET 40
# hand-asserted rows: `requests:` here lists Request::Resize(rows, cols), which the shared parser does not know. Run these through tests/modes.rs by hand.
# D2' (lead, after the #8 adversarial run): with ?40 set DECCOLM does xterm's clear/home/margin reset and records the mode, and asks
#   the host with Request::Resize, but never resizes the grid: the view/PTY width is the single source of truth (vttest leaves ?40
#   set and terminfo is2/rs2 send `CSI ? 3 l`, so a resizing DECCOLM desynced the grid from the window).
# xterm (charproc.c L7559..L7589, set_column_mode L7463): `if (screen->c132) { ClearScreen unless NOCLEAR_COLM; RequestResize (window op);
#   set/clear IN132COLUMNS; xterm_ResetDouble; resetMargins (top/bottom AND left/right); CursorSet(0,0,flags) }`. With c132 FALSE (default; ?40 reset) the
#   whole arm is skipped: no clear, no home, no margin reset, no flag change. ?95 (DECNCSM) is honoured only at vtXX_level >= 5 (xterm default decTerminalID 420 = level 4) so it is ignored.
#   kitty: DECSET 3 clears + homes (screen_erase_in_display 2 + cursor 1,1) but never resizes; DECRST 3 does nothing but store (screen.c L2044). Alacritty: DECCOLM reports NotSupported and ignores
#   (term/mod.rs L2085). Ghostty: ignored unless ?40 (`enable_mode_3`); when enabled resizes to 132/80, eraseDisplay(complete), setCursorPos(1,1) (Terminal.zig deccolm).

#  66    kbd.application_keypad (DECNKM) true          false                     RESET (false)  false          [XT] dpmodes L7772 `MODE_DECKPAM` -- same flag as ESC = / ESC >. NOT in the issue text: add (one arm).
#  5     reverse_video      true                       false                     untouched      false          [XT] dpmodes L7590 REVERSE_VIDEO; ReallyReset full `xw->flags = initflags` (L14510)

#  4(SM) insert             true                       false                     RESET (false)  false          [XT] modes() INSERT; L14550
#  20(SM) linefeed_newline  true                       false                     untouched      false          [XT] L7419; L14510 initflags
#  12    cursor_blink       true (only if the blink resource lets it: SettableCursorBlink) false   RESET (false)  false   [XT] dpmodes L7626 srm_ATT610_BLINK `set_bool_mode(screen->cursor_blink_esc)`; ReallyReset common L14382 `cursor_blink_esc = 0`. ADD to the soft_reset list in lib.rs/csi.rs.
#  25    cursor_visible     true                       false                     SET (true)     true           [XT] L7650; L14378 `cursor_set = ON`
#  40    allow_column_change true                      false                     untouched      untouched      [XT] L7672 c132 is a RESOURCE, not in flags: ReallyReset never writes it
#  47    alt_screen         see ALT block              see ALT block             untouched      false (+clear) [XT] L7759
#  1047  alt_screen         see ALT block              see ALT block             untouched      false (+clear) [XT] L7746
#  1048  (saved cursor)     DECSC                      DECRC                     untouched      n/a            [XT] L7915
#  1049  alt_screen         see ALT block              see ALT block             untouched      false (+clear) [XT] L7732
#  2004  bracketed_paste    true                       false                     untouched      false          [XT] dpmodes L7956 paste_brackets; ReallyReset full L14524 `paste_brackets = OFF`
#  1004  focus_events       true (nothing is sent)     false                     untouched      false          [XT] L7829 flag only; L14441 `send_focus_pos = OFF`
#  9     mouse=X10          exclusive tracking         ANY reset of 9/1000/1001/1002/1003 -> None   untouched   None   [XT] L7613 set_mousemode; really_set_mousemode L7432 `send_mouse_pos = enabled ? mode : MOUSE_OFF`
#  1000  mouse=Normal       "                          "                         untouched      None           [XT] L7807
#  1001  (hilite; not in MouseTracking) ignore + trace "                         untouched      None           [XT] L7811; recommend NOT modelled (needs the hilite dance with the app)
#  1002  mouse=Button       "                          "                         untouched      None           [XT] L7815
#  1003  mouse=AnyMotion    "                          "                         untouched      None           [XT] L7819
#  1005  mouse_encoding=Utf8   exclusive encoding      only if it names the active one -> Default   untouched   Default   [XT] L7832..L7842 `if (IsSM()) extend_coords = code; else if (extend_coords == code) extend_coords = 0`
#  1006  mouse_encoding=Sgr    "                       "                         untouched      Default        [XT] same arm
#  1015  mouse_encoding=Urxvt  "                       "                         untouched      Default        [XT] same arm
#  1016  mouse_encoding=SgrPixels "                    "                         untouched      Default        [XT] same arm
#  2026  synchronized_output  true                    false                     see D-2026     see D-2026     [CNT] synchronized-output.md; xterm patch 411 does NOT implement it (no 2026 in charproc.c nor ctlseqs)
#
#  CORRECTION to the brief: xterm does NOT apply the 'reset only when it names the active one' rule to the TRACKING modes (9/1000/1002/1003) -- only to the
#  ENCODING modes (1005/1006/1015/1016). `CSI ? 1000 h CSI ? 1003 h CSI ? 1000 l` leaves xterm with tracking OFF. Alacritty only clears the matching flag
#  (term/mod.rs L2016..L2023); kitty/WezTerm/Ghostty: unverified. See D-MOUSERESET.
#
#  Unknown / ignored with a trace (xterm has them, Tessera does not model them): 2 (DECANM: `CSI ? 2 l` enters VT52 mode in xterm -- DO NOT implement; ignore), 8 DECARM,
#  10, 13, 14, 18, 19, 30, 35, 38, 41, 42, 44, 45 (#97), 67 DECBKM, 69 DECLRMM (#97), 80 DECSDM, 95 DECNCSM (honoured only at VT510 level), 1001, 1007 (alternate scroll),
#  1010..1014, 1034..1046, 1050..1061, 2001..2003, 2005..2007, 7727. 1007 note: kitty/WezTerm/Alacritty/iTerm2 implement it (wheel -> arrow keys on the alt screen); it belongs to #12.

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- Keyboard modes (hand-asserted: keyboard_modes())
# Format: feed -> expected KeyboardModes {cursor, keypad, mok, kitty}. "default" = {false,false,Disabled,empty}.
# kitty stack model (kitty/screen.c L2145..L2170, ghostty kitty/key.zig FlagStack): a stack of up to N entries per screen; "current" = top entry, flags 0 when empty.
#   push v: append (evict the OLDEST when full) ; pop n: remove up to n entries (n >= depth -> empty -> flags 0) ; set: modifies the top entry (creates one if empty).
#   N: kitty 8 (screen.h L173 `uint8_t main_key_encoding_flags[8], alt_key_encoding_flags[8]`), ghostty 8 (kitty/key.zig `const len = 8`), Alacritty 4096 (term/mod.rs L48).
#   The kitty DOCS only say "Terminals should limit the size of the stack ... the oldest entry must be evicted" -- no number is documented. See D-STACKDEPTH.

# Kitty keyboard stack. Script, expected kitty_flags (bits: 1 disambiguate, 2 event types, 4 alternate keys, 8 all keys as escape codes, 16 associated text)
#  id                       script                                                   expected flags   source
#  KITTY01_push             CSI > 1 u                                                 1                [KT-doc] 'CSI > flags u  # for push'
#  KITTY02_push_default     CSI > u                                                   0 (depth 1)      [KT-doc] 'if flags omitted default to zero'; kitty vt-parser L1397 CALL_CSI_HANDLER1(push, 0); ghostty stream.zig L2679
#  KITTY03_push_push_pop    CSI > 1 u CSI > 3 u CSI < u                               1                [KT-doc] pop defaults to 1
#  KITTY04_pop_empty        CSI < u                                                   0                [KT-doc] 'If a pop request is received that empties the stack, all flags are reset'
#  KITTY05_pop_99           CSI > 1 u CSI > 2 u CSI < 99 u                            0 (stack empty)  [KT-doc]; kitty screen_pop_key_encoding_flags L2162 (loop stops when no active entry); ghostty FlagStack.pop (n >= len resets)
#  KITTY06_pop_0            CSI > 1 u CSI > 2 u CSI < 0 u                             2 (no-op)        kitty L2163 `num && ...` pops nothing for 0; ghostty stream.zig L2687 passes 0 -> pop(0). DECISION D-POP0: recommend no-op (NOT 'default 1'): both reference implementations pop nothing.
#  KITTY07_set_replace      CSI = 5 u                                                 5                [KT-doc] mode 1 default: 'all set bits are set and all unset bits are reset'
#  KITTY08_set_or           CSI = 5 u CSI = 2 ; 2 u                                   7                [KT-doc] mode 2
#  KITTY09_set_andnot       CSI = 7 u CSI = 2 ; 3 u                                   5                [KT-doc] mode 3
#  KITTY10_set_no_params    CSI = 7 u CSI = u                                         0                kitty vt-parser L1393 CALL_CSI_HANDLER2(set, 0, 1): flags default 0, mode default 1 -> replace with 0
#  KITTY11_set_bad_mode     CSI = 7 u CSI = 1 ; 4 u                                   7 (ignored)      kitty screen_set_key_encoding_flags handles how 1,2,3 only; ghostty logs 'invalid setKittyKeyboard command'
#  KITTY12_set_modifies_top CSI > 1 u CSI = 3 ; 2 u CSI < u                           0                kitty screen_set_key_encoding_flags: set edits the top entry (index 0 when the stack is empty); popping it empties the stack
#  KITTY13_mask_bits        CSI > 255 u                                               31 (0x1f)        brief ('flags outside bits 0-4 are masked'); kitty masks `val & 0x7f` (bits 5,6 stored but unused); ghostty IGNORES the whole push when the value does not fit 5 bits. DECISION D-KITTYMASK: recommend mask to 0x1f (brief).
#  KITTY14_depth_cap        push 1..9 (CSI > n u, n=1..9) then pop 1 eight times       after 9 pushes flags 9; after 8 pops flags 0 AND the oldest (1) was evicted: kitty/ghostty depth 8. With the brief's 32 the 33rd push evicts. Fixture uses depth parameter N: assert eviction at N+1.
#  KITTY15_per_screen       CSI > 1 u ; CSI ? 1049 h ; (flags 0) ; CSI > 2 u ; (flags 2) ; CSI ? 1049 l   -> flags 1    [KT-doc] 'main and alternate screens ... separate stacks'; kitty screen_toggle_screen_buffer swaps key_encoding_flags pointers and clears neither; alacritty swap_alt swaps the stacks
#  KITTY16_alt_stack_survives_reentry  CSI ? 1049 h ; CSI > 2 u ; CSI ? 1049 l ; CSI ? 1049 h   -> flags 2 (alt stack kept across visits)   kitty (arrays kept); alacritty inactive stack kept. Tessera's Grid stashes lines but the keyboard stacks live in Terminal state, so this is automatic; do NOT clear the alt stack on 1049 set.
#  KITTY17_decstr           CSI > 3 u CSI ? 1049 h CSI > 4 u CSI ! p                  main 0, alt 0    kitty do_screen_reset memsets both stacks (also hard reset). Not in the kitty doc.
#  KITTY18_ris              same then ESC c                                           0 / 0            kitty do_screen_reset; xterm n/a
#  KITTY19_query_not_here   CSI ? u                                                   no state change  query reply is #10 (`CSI ? flags u`); must not push/pop. Negative.
#  KITTY20_private_markers  CSI < u / CSI > u / CSI = u / CSI ? u are four different functions; plain `CSI u` (no marker, no params) is SCORC/DECRC (#94) and must NOT touch the stack. `CSI 5 u` with a param and no marker: ignored (kitty vt-parser L1382 requires !num_params for restore).
#
#  Not covered by the table: XTMODKEYS Pp != 4 (ignored), `CSI > Pp n` (XTMODKEYS disable; unimplemented, ignore).

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- app-core: bracketed paste and focus (table; tests live in tessera-app-core with the fake PTY)
# Source for wrapper bytes: [CTL] "Bracketed Paste Mode ... ESC [ 2 0 0 ~ / ESC [ 2 0 1 ~" (PASTE_IN_BRACKET ?2004, 'CSI ? 2004 h'), [XT] charproc.c L7955, button.c L2835/L2877.
#   input event                         modes                 bytes written to the PTY                                     source / note
#   Paste "hi"                          2004 off              hi                                                           existing behaviour
#   Paste "hi"                          2004 on               ESC[200~ hi ESC[201~                                         [CTL]; wezterm term/terminalstate/mod.rs L943..L966; alacritty event.rs L1376..L1389; kitty window.py L2412
#   Paste "a\nb" / "a\r\nb"             2004 off              a CR b                                                       existing sanitize_paste (LF/CRLF -> CR)
#   Paste "a\nb"                        2004 on               DECISION D-PASTENL. Today's sanitize_paste would give a CR b inside the brackets. wezterm: NewlineCanon::None (text untouched) when bracketed; alacritty: untouched; kitty: untouched; xterm: untouched. Recommend: keep the text's line breaks as LF inside the brackets (apps like vim/zsh treat LF as a real newline in a paste; CR would be interpreted as Enter by some readline setups). Needs a second sanitiser path (`sanitize_paste(text, bracketed)`); unverified how zsh treats CR inside brackets.
#   Paste "x ESC[201~ y"                2004 on               ESC[200~ x y ESC[201~  (recommended) / ESC[200~ x[201~y ESC[201~ (what today's sanitiser yields)   ESC is a control character; sanitize_paste ALREADY drops every `char::is_control` (ESC, C1 incl. U+009B, DEL, C0 except TAB/CR/LF) so the end marker cannot be forged: the issue's "also strip ESC[201~" is already satisfied for safety. Cosmetic: wezterm strips the WHOLE `ESC[200~`/`ESC[201~` (also when not bracketed), kitty strips `ESC[201~` and `CSI(0x9b)201~` repeatedly, alacritty strips only ESC and ETX (0x03) leaving `[201~`. Recommend a pre-pass removing the full ESC[200~ / ESC[201~ (cheap, nicer text), then the existing control filter.
#   Paste "a ETX b" (0x03)              2004 on               ETX removed by is_control                                    alacritty strips 0x03 explicitly because some shells end the paste on it; already covered.
#   Paste "" (empty)                    2004 on               ESC[200~ ESC[201~                                            xterm wraps unconditionally; unverified for others. Recommend wrap (or send nothing); either safe. DECISION left to implementer; fixture asserts the wrapper.
#   Paste with 2004 toggled mid-flight  the decision uses modes() read under the same lock as the write buffer; a paste sees one consistent value.
#   Focus(true)                         1004 on               ESC[I                                                        [CTL] 'Ps = 1004 -> Send FocusIn/FocusOut events'; focus reports are CSI I / CSI O
#   Focus(false)                        1004 on               ESC[O
#   Focus(true) / Focus(false)          1004 off              (nothing)
#   DECSET 1004 while the window is focused   -             (nothing)                                                     [XT] charproc.c L7829: the arm only stores the flag; xterm does not report the current state on enable (kitty/WezTerm/alacritty also do not). Answer to the brief's question: no immediate report.
#   Focus(true) twice                   1004 on               ESC[I once (recommended: report TRANSITIONS only) — xterm reports each X event, which are already transitions; AppKit can deliver duplicates, so de-duplicate in app-core. DECISION D-FOCUSDEDUP.
#   Focus(true) while 1004 set later    set 1004 after focus   (nothing until the next change)

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- 2026 synchronized output
#   `CSI ? 2026 h` / `CSI ? 2026 l` store Modes.synchronized_output only [CNT]. xterm patch 411 does not implement it; kitty, WezTerm, Alacritty (0.13+: queues, 150 ms), Ghostty, iTerm2, Contour do.
#   Spec gaps (the Contour write-up is explicitly 'informal'): no timeout value, nothing about set-while-set (idempotent), RIS/DECSTR, alt-screen switch.
#   DECISION D-2026: recommend RIS and DECSTR both reset it to false (a program that crashed between BSU and ESU must not freeze the screen after `reset`/`tput init`, which send DECSTR);
#   alt-screen switches leave it alone; the app-core 1 s cap (brief D3) stays the safety net. Unverified against other emulators.

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- vttest screens in csi_spec.txt `#### DEFERRED ... -> #8`
# Evidence: the wave-3 vttest captures (…/scratchpad/wave3/csi/vttest_capture/m*_*.bin, vttest 2.7 20251205) were grepped for DEC private sequences:
#   m1_02 [?3h | m1_03 [3;21r [?3l x2 [?6h [?6l [r | m1_04 [3;21r [?3h [?6h [?6l [r | m2_03 [?3h [?5h | m2_04 [?3l | m2_05 [?3h [?5l | m2_06 [?3l
#   m2_07 [12;13r [?4h [?6h | m2_08 [1;24r | m2_09 [12;13r [?4l | m2_10 [1;24r | m2_11 [23;24r | m2_12 [?6l | m2_13 [1;24r [?5l | m2_14 [?5h | m2_15 [?5l | m8_02 [2;23r [?6h [?6l [r | m8_03 [4h [4l | m8_08 [?3h

#   screen                         verdict with DECCOLM ignored (c132 off)           why

#   V2S4_80col_light_background    LIFT (passes today too)                           stream = ?3l, ED 2, text; ?5h belongs to the PREVIOUS screen (m2_03), DECSCNM is not rendered
#   V2S6_80col_dark_background     LIFT (passes today too)                           same with ?3l

#   V2S14_light_background_prompt  LIFT                                              ?5h is stored only; text 'Light background. Push <RETURN>' identical
#   V8S2_accordion_original_DECOM  LIFT                                              ?6h, DECSTBM 2;23, [r, ?6l; expected screen present

To lift them later: add a harness step feeding ESC[?40h first and expect 132-column screens (needs `size_after`-style assertion; ~7 wide screens).

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- esctest `#>` rows

#   E_DECRC_saveRestoreCursor_wrap        LIFT: `DECSET 7; DECSC; DECRST 7; DECRC; CUP(79,1); abcd` -> cursor on row 1 (see DECOM24: with the @set seam replaced by ESC[?7l)

#   E_VPA_ignoresOriginMode, E_HPA_ignoresOriginMode, E_CUP_respectsOriginMode, E_HVP_respectsOriginMode, E_CHA_respectsOriginMode, E_HPR/VPR_ignoresOriginMode   STAY -> #97 (all set DECLRMM).
#     NOTE on E_VPA_ignoresOriginMode: xterm's code makes VPA origin-relative (DECOM11); the esctest passes because its assertion reads the cursor back through CPR, which xterm reports origin-relative. Tessera has no CPR yet (#10). Do not lift as a 'VPA ignores DECOM' claim.

Lifting them verbatim is optional.
#   V2S14 lifts as above.

# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- DECISIONS (recommendation first)
#   D-VPA         VPA (and HPA/VPR/HPR) go through the same origin-aware positioning as CUP: relative to the region under DECOM (DECOM11/12/13).
#   D-AWMPEND     DECRST/DECSET 7 does not touch a pending wrap (xterm, today's behaviour; DEC STD 070 p5-139 says reset clears it). AWM04.
#   D-ALTREPEAT   1049 set while already on alt: clear again + overwrite the alt saved-cursor slot (xterm). kitty/alacritty: strict no-op. ALT03.
#   D-1049MAIN    1049 reset while on main: NO-OP (kitty/alacritty), deviating from xterm (jumps to the saved/home position and clears DECOM/attrs). ALT04.
#   D-ALTCUR      47/1047 leave: cursor, pen and pending wrap stay as they were on the alt screen (xterm, esctest 'cursor should not move'); Grid::leave_alt_screen restores the primary's, so the Terminal must re-apply (or a Grid variant). 1049 restores via DECRC. ALT05.
#   D-ALT47       47 does not preserve alt contents across visits in Tessera (fresh blank each entry; alacritty does the same): documented divergence from xterm. ALT07.
#   D-ALTSLOT     Grid keeps the alternate screen's saved cursor across entries (xterm), so E_DECRC_..._altVsMain passes. ALT10.
#   D-MOUSERESET  Reset of ANY tracking mode (9/1000/1002/1003) -> MouseTracking::None (xterm); encodings reset only when naming the active one. The brief's wording applies to encodings only. MOUSE02/03.
#   D-STACKDEPTH  Kitty stack depth: kitty and Ghostty use 8 (source, not documented; Alacritty 4096). Lead D6 says 'use kitty's number': recommend 8, not the brief's 32.
#   D-KITTYMASK   Mask flags to 0x1f (brief). kitty masks 0x7f; Ghostty rejects the whole command above 31. KITTY13.
#   D-POP0        `CSI < 0 u` pops nothing (kitty and Ghostty); `CSI < u` pops 1; `CSI < 99 u` empties the stack and leaves flags 0. KITTY05/06.
#   D-MOKRANGE    `CSI > 4 ; Pv m` with Pv > 2: ignore. `CSI > 4 m` and `CSI > m` reset to Disabled. KBD04/05.
#   D-RISCOLS     RIS in 132-column mode: resize back to 80 and push Request::Resize(rows, 80) (xterm RequestResize); or leave to the host. COL09 (unverified).
#   D-2026        RIS and DECSTR reset ?2026 (spec silent).
#   D-PASTENL     Under 2004 keep line breaks as-is (all four reference emulators); today's sanitiser converts them to CR. Needs the lead's call; changes current behaviour.
#   D-FOCUSDEDUP  Report focus transitions only; setting ?1004 sends nothing.
#   ADD to scope:  ?66 (DECNKM = DECKPAM flag, xterm), ?12 reset by DECSTR, a negative test that `CSI ? 4 h` is not IRM (PRIV01), DECSTR/RIS also reset the soft items listed in the DECSTR table above, `CSI ? 2 l` (VT52) must stay ignored.
